summary: A member asked for their vote on a bill says they have not decided yet and names what they are waiting on: the bill read through, the floor debate, a change they asked for, or something in return.
realLife: Before a North Carolina House override vote in December 2024, Rep. Mike Clampitt told a reporter: "I'm not going to say where I'm at yet because I'm still undecided... [When] I get closer to time, I'll have to make a decision." Rep. Mark Pless said he had asked for part of the bill to be changed and been told no, and would see what arguments colleagues made on the floor before deciding; the reporter wrote that another holdout could be trying to extract concessions from leadership in exchange for his vote.
sources: Bryan Anderson, "GOP holdouts remain undecided on forthcoming vote to strip powers of incoming Democrats," The Caucus, Dec 6, 2024: https://thecaucus.substack.com/p/gop-holdouts-sb-382
inGame: The scene-talk arcs ask-vote, hearing-ask and cosponsor-ask: the one asked answers not yet (asks.carried) where a favor would carry them, and says what would.

turns.summary: Asked again, or given what they named, the member says yes.
pulledBy: a plea from someone they owe
turns.writesBack: Their vote is counted for the bill, and the favor is owed.

turns.summary: The member still will not say, and decides on the floor.
pulledBy: a change they asked for and were refused
turns.writesBack: The count stays open until the roll call.

turns.summary: Nothing they waited on arrives, and the member votes no.
turns.writesBack: The vote goes against the bill, and the asker remembers who held out.
